blocks.text: LUCENA CITY – Taal Volcano recorded four volcanic earthquakes and lower sulfur dioxide (SO₂) emissions in the past 24 hours, indicating continued seismic calm, the Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (Phivolcs) reported on Tuesday, The latest monitoring results reflect a decline in seismic activity compared with previous days. The volcano registered eight volcanic earthquakes on November 23, three on November 22, 11 on November 21, and 13 on November 20. READ: Taal volcano’s gas emissions rise as earthquakes decline Meanwhile, sulfur dioxide (SO₂) emissions from Taal Volcano also dropped significantly during the latest monitoring period.
